# How Skills-Based Hiring Can Transform Your Organization In 2025

By Stacie Garland

Share

If traditional hiring practices are increasingly proving to do more harm than good in recruitment, does this explain why skills-based hiring is on the rise?

The labor market isn’t what it was a decade ago. Today, traditional recruitment processes, like resume scanning and experience-based hiring, aren’t as effective for gauging a candidate’s fit for a position. In fact, some of these practices can be considered unreliable for candidate assessment.

There are many reasons for this discrepancy, but traditional hiring practices that consider education and degrees as a predictor of success are proving to be a big obstacle for companies seeking to recruit top talent.

Instead of relying on outdated recruitment tools, skills-based hiring is emerging as the best alternative to close skill gaps, retain employees and reduce the chances of making a bad hire – but how exactly does it work?

## What is skills-based hiring or a skills first approach?

If you’re unfamiliar with the philosophy, skills-based hiring is the practice of screening and hiring new employees based on the skills, capabilities, and talent they bring to the table — as opposed to their educational background or degree.

Skills-based hiring considers soft skills and hard skills to screen in candidates, rather than eliminating qualified applicants because they don’t have the right background on paper. The easiest way to implement skill-based hiring is through job skills testing, which is otherwise known as an employee skills assessment.

Some companies choose to integrate skill assessments early in the screening process to ensure that they’re spending time focusing on those candidates uniquely qualified to perform.

In contrast, others use it during the later stages of the recruitment funnel, particularly when trying to identify the best candidate from a shortlist of two or three applicants.

## What makes skills-based recruitment different from other types?

In a typical hiring process, screening tools and tactics look for keywords on an application to verify if the candidate is suitable for the role. In theory, these screening practices seek to ensure the candidate is the “right fit”, using an applicant’s education or degree as a proxy for talent.

However, this approach to hiring can be misleading for a variety of reasons. Firstly, resumes are unreliable at best, since many candidates may inflate their experience or outright lie.

Secondly, a degree doesn’t necessarily tell you if a candidate is capable of performing well, as their qualifications may not reflect their actual abilities – but why is this discrepancy important?

Well, many recruiters look at a candidate’s resume, see the computer science degree, and assume the candidate has the skills required to do the job. At the other end of the spectrum, a recruiter will often dismiss an engineer’s self-taught coding skills because they don’t come with the right pedigree or certification.

Ultimately, failing to make hiring decisions based on skills risks recruiters missing out on great employees, just because a candidate doesn’t get the chance to prove what they can do. In addition, using skills as a metric to measure talent also encourages data driven decisions during the hiring process.

[Read more: What are hard skills]

## Why more companies are implementing skills first hiring processes

Hiring people based on skills allows recruiters to see if a candidate is truly equipped to do the job — helping them make the best hire the first time around. This is especially relevant in an era when many companies are facing a skills gap in their workforce.

As an example, the rising skills gap will see key industries like technology, media, and telecommunications fall short 4.3 million workers by 2030. In total, these shortages are predicted to cost this industry alone an eye-watering $449.7 billion in unrealized revenue.

Skill-based hiring allows companies to consider less “traditional” candidates: a former bartender, for instance, certainly has the customer service skills to work in a call center.

[Try Our Free Skills Gap Analysis Template]

It’s important to note that skills based hiring is a two pronged approach. Hard skills are specific technical skills and training, while soft skills relate to traits like leadership or communication.

In contrast, soft skills are highly valued across industries — but they can be difficult to screen for during the hiring process. Things like education, extracurricular activities, or leadership positions are often used by recruiters as a proxy for sought-after soft skills.

Unfortunately, these so-called predictors of soft skills can be discriminatory, preventing minorities and other diverse candidates from proving their abilities.

For groups that are often shut out of leadership positions and traditional institutions, it’s difficult to show soft skills in a two-dimensional application, like a cover letter or CV.

## Why legislation is encouraging employee skills testing

Despite their benefits, in-demand soft skills are often assessed via personality tests, which have since been debunked as pseudoscience by Dr Sarah Gaither, an assistant professor of psychology and neuroscience at Duke University. Not only have these been proven as false indicators of success, but they may actually be illegal.

Bias tied to age, gender, race, religion, and more is pervasive in workplaces worldwide. In organizations, it’s all too easy to consciously or subconsciously include these biases in talent acquisition software, creating inequalities at every stage of the employment cycle.

What’s more, is that some forms of psychometric testing, such as personality tests, lack the proper validation required to be compliant with the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC).

In addition, new legislation being introduced across the United States, in particular New York City, is soon to restrict employers from using recruitment screening tools powered by artificial intelligence.

As these changes would suggest, governments are increasingly moving towards legislation that encourages skills-based hiring to help combat systematic inequalities, and provide the same opportunities to people from all walks of life.

To make efficient and discretionary decision-making while still staying compliant, job simulations are one of the few skills assessment tools that will help companies to adhere to the relevant legislation while still having the tools to hire top talent.

## 3 key benefits of skills-based hiring

Ultimately, figuring out how to adopt skills-based hiring practices allows companies to achieve a number of high caliber goals in one simple philosophy.

Skill-based hiring helps lower recruiting costs by ensuring hiring managers bring on the right new employee the first time around — thereby avoiding the costs of a bad hire. It also enables companies to close skill gaps, improve retention, and increase productivity with people who are truly equipped to perform well.

By embracing employee skills testing as a key recruitment strategy, other noteworthy benefits of adopting this approach include the following.

### Hire with confidence

Employee skills assessments are the easiest way to practice skill-based hiring, as a job skill test provides an unbiased, validated evaluation of a candidate’s ability to perform the duties listed in the job description. Using a series of questions in different formats, candidates are able to show how they would approach the role.

Depending on the nature of the role, questions can be immersive, such as a coding challenge or job simulation, or target soft skills: things like motivation, communication, and emotional intelligence. Alternatively, companies can combine both into a role specific job skills test as well.

Skill assessments level the playing field for all candidates. More so than resumes or job interviews, a skills test can assess the true potential of a new hire to go the distance with the company while giving all applicants an equal opportunity to showcase their talents.

More intense skill assessments, like job auditions, are another great way to predict job performance. Job auditions can take a few forms. Some organizations utilize a case study, while others will host a group interview or event. At Vervoe, we combine these formats into a unique skills testing tool called job simulations.

[Read More: Why Job Simulations Are The New, Predictive Way To Hire]

### Improve diversity hiring

Research shows that skill-testing can help companies overcome unconscious bias and improve diversity hiring. Rather than using shortcuts like education or job titles, skill assessments allow companies to tap into a wider, more diverse talent pool.

While promoting the concept of skills-based hiring, Harvard Business Review told organizations to focus on the results that they would like to see, rather than the type of qualifications that they think could potentially deliver them.

“Start by rethinking your job descriptions. Highlighting the desired skills — the candidate’s ability to perform certain tasks — gets to the same results without creating an unnecessary barrier to entry, like a requirement for a four-year degree.”

By including candidates who have obtained their trade through alternative education methods, job skill testing can help companies reach their diversity hiring goals, which leads to a whole other host of benefits including increased innovation, productivity, and profitability.

### Boost employee retention

Skill-based hiring aims to replicate the experience of working in the actual role the candidate will be hired for. For example, a marketer may be asked to present a strategy proposal. A UX designer might be asked to review a user flow within a product. A sales representative might be asked to write a cold outreach email.

For new hires, skill-based hiring provides the opportunity to try the role on for size. Candidates can then self-select out of the hiring process if they feel they aren’t a good fit. Inevitably, the candidate who is hired is not only a better fit for the role — they’re also excited to take on the day-to-day responsibilities.

More diverse candidates who are hired via skill-based hiring also tend to stay longer. According to LinkedIn, employees without a traditional four-year degree stay at companies 34% longer than those with such a degree, making them ideal choices for companies looking to boost retention.

In fact, the data shows that candidates also enjoy the opportunity to show their skills. Companies that use Vervoe’s assessments experience a 97% candidate completion rate, which is among the highest engagement rates in the industry.

## A skills first approach makes life easier for recruiters

Many HR teams receive hundreds of resumes for a single open position. It’s nearly impossible to give every candidate’s application careful consideration, which leads many recruiters to simply select the candidates whose backgrounds seem most familiar or similar to theirs.

Thankfully, skills-based hiring helps to reduce the strain on recruiters, and help them to hire at scale. Vervoe uses machine learning to screen candidates in, not out, and our AI powered platform uses a unique, efficient multi-layered approach to match candidates with the preferences of the employer.

The algorithm allows HR teams to evaluate 10,000 candidates in the same time it takes for an individual recruiter to assess one. Recruiters receive a shortlist of top candidates who performed well related to the entire application pool — and no one is disqualified from continuing on in the process.

[Read more: Recruitment skills]

## Can your company afford not to adopt employee skills testing?

Skill-based hiring doesn’t require a huge investment in time or resources — on the contrary, skill-testing can actually save recruiters money and effort. This approach is also an incredibly easy way to fill skill gaps in an extremely competitive hiring market, enabling candidates who may not have a traditional background to shine.

By considering factors other than education, skill-based hiring allows recruiting teams to find the right combination of hard and soft skills to fill every open position. # 7 Candidate Screening Methods for Better Hiring

By Raji Oluwaniyi

Share

Screening candidates is fundamentally the core of any recruitment process. As such, it's important to ensure that your screening is comprehensive enough to identify the most talented applicants within the shortest time possible.

With the right candidate screening techniques, you can hire the best talent and close any skill gaps, ensuring your company has the talent it needs to achieve its goals. In this article, we will explore 7 candidate evaluation techniques and explain how you can implement each one.

But, before we get into it…

## What is candidate screening?

Candidate screening encompasses all hiring processes that evaluate a job candidate’s skills, competencies, and experience. The results of this screening show how fit a candidate is for a particular role at a company.

Screening candidates is the second stage of hiring, after sourcing candidates, which aims to narrow the applicant pool to identify the most suitable candidates for the role. This process can involve using tests, questions in the application, or even interviews to assess how qualified the candidates are for the job.

The candidate screening process is crucial, as hiring the wrong person can lead to skills gaps, misaligned roles, and diminished company performance. With 75% of employers companies admitting to making this mistake, it’s essential to implement a comprehensive evaluation process to avoid similar pitfalls.

The good news is that there are multiple candidate screening techniques you can apply to find the perfect fit for your company, including skills testing, resume screening, and trial projects. You can combine these methods to build your evaluation process and ensure you hire right each time.

## 1. Skills testing

Put simply, skills testing is a candidate evaluation technique where companies measure the candidates’ skills using pre-designed assessments. These tests can be designed in text, audio, multiple-choice, or a combination of any of these formats to assess applicants for the skills vital to the position thoroughly.

Comprehensive skills testing and talent assessment provide an effective way to identify candidates with the skills your company needs and evaluate them for culture fit and culture add. This candidate screening technique is also extremely versatile and can be applied to your recruitment in many ways. For example, although nearly 70% of recruiters apply skills testing at the top of their hiring funnel, you can use it at the middle or end of the process, depending on your goals.

## Types of skills tests

Skills tests are a powerful tool for gauging different capabilities required for a role, including soft skills and technical skills. These tests differ from one another in the way questions are structured and the type of skills they evaluate. Let’s go over the different types of skills tests and what differentiates them from the rest:

- Technical skills tests: These evaluate the candidate’s proficiency in role-specific skills, which require more technical knowledge of various concepts. Technical skills tests check for capabilities like proficiency in programming languages for software developers and copywriting skills for marketing professionals.

- Cognitive skills tests: As the name implies, cognitive ability tests are designed to measure candidates' reasoning skills, memory, and critical thinking. These tests check how well the applicants can process information, learn new concepts, and adapt to different situations, all of which are vital for excellent job performance.

- Soft skills tests: These assessments evaluate interpersonal skills like communication and collaboration as well as leadership and situational judgment skills. They also include tests for personality and culture add or fit to see if the candidate has the traits your company seeks.

### How to run a skills test

Knowing what a skills test entails is one thing, but understanding how to do it right ensures you get the best results from your hiring each time. Here are the steps to effectively run a skills test:

1. Identify the skills you want to test for

Start by defining the goal of your assessment process. This could either be to close skill gaps within your company or to fill specific roles. In alignment with this, you can then spot the skills your company or the role requires. This serves as the foundation for building your skill assessment to assist in screening applicants.

Then, for each identified skill, work with stakeholders and high performers to define what "good" looks like in practice for the role. This creates clear benchmarks for assessment and helps ensure you're evaluating candidates against realistic standards for success in the role.

2. Select an excellent testing platform

When choosing your assessment tool, be sure to look out for extensive features and pricing options that align with your budget. The ideal testing platform should also provide an assessment library with a variety of tests to evaluate the soft and technical skills required for various roles.

3. Set up your assessment

Now, you can decide the types of tests you want to use and how you plan to combine them to assess each candidate's fit for the job. For example, if you’re hiring a Social Media Manager, you can apply technical assessments that assess their ability to use content management platforms like scheduling tools. To make the assessment even more comprehensive, you can combine these with collaboration and content writing skills tests.

4. Perform a test run and administer the assessment

Before deploying the test to candidates, run it with team members to identify any ambiguities or technical glitches. Once it’s tested, you can administer it to your candidates. However, be sure to provide clear instructions on how the assessment will be scored, the time limits, and the purpose of the test.

## Pros & cons of skills testing

Pros

- Allows for objective skills evaluation

- It helps identify top candidates faster

- Provides a bias-free way to assess skills

- Offers a uniform method to screen candidates with the same metrics

Cons

- Skills tests can be high-pressure, but they spotlight skills that don’t show on resumes alone

- Standardized tests can feel rigid; however, customizable assessments leave room for diversity

## 2. Resume screening

Resume screening is the process of evaluating applicants’ resumes, either manually or with the help of screening software, to identify candidates who align with a role's requirements. By reviewing details like education, work experience, skills, and certifications, you can easily pinpoint candidates for further consideration.

- Often the first step in hiring, resume screening helps you identify top talent while getting insights into how well candidates can present themselves. However, it isn’t completely reliable, as over 62% of job applicants admit to falsifying information on their resumes. To improve its effectiveness, consider using an applicant tracking system (ATS) alongside other screening methods, such as skills testing, to ensure a more accurate evaluation.

## How to run a resume review

Adding resume reviews to your screening strategy can help you identify qualified candidates and ensure they align with your job requirements. In this section, we will explore how to assess resumes to spot top talent and avoid common pitfalls:

1. Define the role requirements

Determine the level of proficiency, experience, or qualifications the open role requires. Then, based on your results, create an initial screening process checklist containing standardized categories like education, work experience, and certifications.

2. Sort the resumes

Now, separate the resumes that meet your basic criteria from the ones that don’t. If the resumes were submitted virtually, you can use an Applicant Tracking System to complete this sorting process.

3. Review the resume

During the review stage, look out for past roles and responsibilities that align with the one you’re hiring for. Also, look out for potential red flags such as unexplained employment gaps or generic descriptions. Then, score the candidates based on your review and shortlist those who meet your standards.

Pros & cons of resume screening

Pros

- It focuses on recorded qualifications and experience

- It’s great for initial candidate filtering

Cons

- Leaves room for bias and human errors

- Not a reliable standalone method of verifying skills

- Not suitable for high-volume hiring

## 3. Virtual interview

Virtual interviewing is a modern screening method where interviews are conducted online, often via video conferencing tools like Zoom or Google Meet. Recruiters can also implement video screenings where you ask a question via the job post or a screening platform, and candidates record a video of themselves answering it. This serves as a mini-interview, which you can review afterwards.

These interviews allow you to connect with candidates from anywhere in the world, making the process more flexible and accessible for both parties. This approach is particularly useful for remote or hybrid roles, as well as for saving time and resources in the early stages of hiring. For example, instead of coordinating in-person meetings, you can schedule quick video calls to assess a candidate's communication skills, cultural fit, and qualifications.

### How to run a virtual interview

Running a great virtual interview is about creating a seamless and professional experience for both you and the candidate, regardless of location. Here’s how to do it successfully:

1. Choose the interview format and platform

Start by selecting the type of virtual interview you want, which could be a live interview or pre-recorded videos. Once that’s set, select a reliable video conferencing tool like Zoom, which supports screen sharing and recording.

2. Prepare the interview questions and schedule the interview

Structure the interview with a mix of open-ended, role-specific, and behavioral questions. You can also use questions based on their resume to verify their experience in similar roles. Then, you can schedule the interview for a time convenient for you and the candidate and send an invite.

3. Start with introductions, then proceed to questions

During the interview, begin by giving the candidate an overview of the company. Then, introduce yourself and your role. Provide room for the candidates to introduce themselves too, before the interview questions.

4. Allow candidates to ask questions

After the candidate provides answers to your questions, you should create room for them to ask their questions as well.

If you’re using the video-answer format for your virtual interview, be sure to prepare the questions beforehand and provide enough guidance on how candidates should answer them. Also, ensure that your questions are clear and straightforward. Then, set a time frame for candidates to give their responses so you can review and shortlist them on time.

### Pros & cons of virtual interviews

Pros

- It is convenient for both candidates and recruiters

- It lets you reach candidates from almost any location

- It is cost-effective

Cons

- There are chances for technical issues

- It can be challenging to interpret non-verbal cues

## 4. Job simulations

Job simulations are realistic assessments designed to evaluate a candidate's skills and behaviors in scenarios that mirror actual on-the-job tasks. By immersing candidates in workplace-relevant tasks, you can gain insights into their problem-solving, decision-making, and interpersonal skills.

These simulations often involve role-playing, situational judgment tests, or hands-on activities, allowing candidates to demonstrate their competencies in a practical context. As a result, you identify the best fit for a position and give the candidates a clearer understanding of job expectations.

### How to run a job simulation

The efficiency of your job simulations largely depends on how well you develop and administer them to candidates. Below is a quick guide on how to create and run them effectively:

1. Define your objectives and select a simulation format

First, determine what you want to assess, such as problem-solving abilities, technical skills, or interpersonal communication. Then, select the job simulation format that would work best for achieving your goal. You can either use a testing platform with job simulation capabilities like Vervoe or apply hands-on activities to assess candidate skills.

2. Develop scenarios

Create realistic scenarios that reflect the daily responsibilities of the job. These scenarios should challenge candidates appropriately and align with the skills you’ve identified. Once that’s ready, gather all necessary materials, including instructions and resources candidates will need to complete the simulation. This could include organizational charts or background information relevant to the tasks.

3. Administer the simulation after clearly stating your expectations

Before the job simulation, outline the skills you will assess and how they will be evaluated. Be sure to provide any necessary instructions regarding time commitments as well. After this, you can administer the job simulation to your candidates.

4. Evaluate results and provide feedback

After completing the simulations, assess candidates based on your predefined criteria. You can use a scoring structure to ensure consistency in your evaluations. Once that's done, be sure to let the candidates know how they performed as soon as the results are in, and you’ve made your decision.

### Pros & cons of job simulations

Pros

- Allows candidates to demonstrate their skills in realistic scenarios

- Provides measurable data on candidate performance

- Candidates get a clearer picture of job requirements

- Encourages employee retention

Cons

- Developing simulations can require significant time, but it allows for accurate prediction of job performance

- Complex simulations may deter candidates, but using the right platforms can help ensure concise yet comprehensive assessments.

## 5. Cover letters

Cover letters are a traditional yet effective candidate evaluation technique that provides insight into a candidate’s communication skills, professionalism, and enthusiasm for the role. Unlike resumes, which focus on qualifications, cover letters reveal a candidate’s personality, motivations, and how they align with the company’s values.

They also demonstrate the ability to tailor content to a specific audience, showcasing attention to detail and genuine interest. However, their effectiveness depends on the quality of the content provided by candidates, making them more subjective.

### What to look out for in a cover letter

Cover letters can say a lot about the candidates, from their personality to their work ethic as well. However, to effectively review them, you’d need to look out for some indicators. Here are some things to look out for in a cover letter:

1. An understanding of the role: The cover letter should be customized for the specific job and your company. This demonstrates that the candidate did their research and understands the role. So, keep an eye out for generic letters, which are a red flag.

2. Clear Structure: A good cover letter should have a logical flow. This typically includes an introduction, an explanation of relevant skills, and a closing statement expressing enthusiasm and the next steps.

3. Relevance to the role: In their cover letters, candidates should highlight experiences and skills that directly align with the job description. Be sure to look for examples that illustrate their qualifications and ability to solve problems common to the role.

4. Enthusiasm and personality: The tone should be professional but enthusiastic, reflecting genuine interest in the role and the company. A lack of energy can signal a lack of commitment.

### Pros & cons of cover letters

Pros:

- Enables recruiters to spot motivated candidates easily

- Gives excellent insights into candidates’ personality

- Fills in the gaps in a resume and provides context

Cons

- It can be time-consuming to review

- It can be subjective

## 6. Background checks

Background checks are designed to confirm a candidate’s identity, qualifications, and history. They involve verifying information about a candidate’s education, employment records, criminal history, credit reports, and sometimes even social media activity, depending on the role’s requirements.

You can think of it as fact-checking the details provided on a candidate’s resume and during interviews to ensure they’re accurate and reliable. For instance, verifying a degree ensures the candidate has the academic qualifications for the role, while a criminal records check helps maintain safety and compliance standards. By uncovering any discrepancies, these background checks can help you make informed and confident hiring decisions.

### How to run a background check

Background checks are your safety net for hiring decisions, as they help you uncover crucial details that might not appear on a resume. Here, we will cover the essentials of conducting thorough checks to protect your company and hire right:

1. Understand legal requirements

Before starting, familiarize yourself with privacy laws, such as the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA). Also, be sure to obtain written consent from the candidate to proceed, as most jurisdictions require this to protect privacy rights.

2. Define the scope of the background check

Identify what specific checks you need based on the role and which ones are more important than others. For example, you can prioritize criminal records over education verification. This lets you define dealbreakers in your screening process, enabling you to focus on those that meet all your requirements.

3. Collect and verify the necessary information from the candidate

Now, you can gather key details like the candidate’s full name, date of birth, Social Security number, and previous addresses. Then, confirm the candidate’s identity using the provided information to ensure you are conducting the check on the right person.

4. Run the background check

This process may include searches across databases using people search tools to verify relevant information like employment history. It can also involve reaching out to prior employers to confirm the candidate’s claims.

5. Review the results

Finally, analyze the report for any discrepancies or red flags, such as gaps in employment, unverified degrees, or a criminal history. Consider the relevance of any issues to the role. Once you’re done, be sure to follow up with candidates and let them know the results of the background check.

### Pros & cons of background checks

Pros:

- Verifies the accuracy of resumes and applications

- Helps protect company reputation

- Identifies potential red flags, like fraudulent credentials

Cons:

- Background checks can take time

- Background check tools aren't always accurate

## 7. Trial Projects

Trial projects are short, practical assignments administered to candidates during the hiring process to evaluate their skills, problem-solving abilities, and approach to real-world tasks. Unlike traditional interviews, which often focus on theoretical knowledge or past experiences, trial projects let candidates demonstrate how they’d perform in the actual role.

For example, if you’re hiring a graphic designer, you can ask candidates to create a sample design based on a brief. These projects are ideally tailored to mimic on-the-job tasks, providing insights into a candidate's expertise, creativity, and ability to meet deadlines.

### What to look out for when conducting trial projects

Trial projects require attention to detail and a keen eye for various indicators to determine whether the candidate has all the skills they claim. Here are some things you should look out for when using this screening method:

1. Quality of work: The candidate’s work should align with the project’s objectives and your instructions. It should also be thorough and accurate, showing attention to detail in the deliverables.

2. Problem-Solving Approach: Look beyond the final result and prioritize assessing how the candidate approached the task. Measure how well they used innovative solutions and creative techniques to tackle issues.

3. Time Management: Review whether the project was completed within the allotted timeframe without compromising quality. This indicates how well they can handle deadlines and still drive excellent work.

### Pros & cons of trial projects

Pros:

- Offers candidates hands-on experience of the role’s responsibilities

- Allows for more objective skills evaluation

- Perfect for measuring time-management skills

Cons:

- It can be time-consuming for candidates

- Risk of turning candidates away due to unpaid work

## How to choose a candidate screening method for effective hiring

Selecting the right candidate screening method is important for building an effective team and avoiding costly hiring mistakes. With so many options available, you must identify the ones that align with your company’s goals and know how to implement them for the best results. Here are some key measures to consider:

### 1. Define your hiring goals

The candidate screening method you choose depends on what you want to achieve in your hiring process. For example, if you want a more comprehensive yet flexible candidate assessment, online skills testing would be the perfect fit. Or, if you want to grade candidates based on how well they can adapt to your company’s environment, then a trial project or job simulation would suffice.

Defining your hiring goals beforehand gives your entire candidate screening process a direction. This prevents you from under-evaluating candidate skills and ensures you hire someone that meets your standards.

### 2. Outline the skills the open role needs

Once you have your hiring goals set, determine and outline the skills the open role needs as a guide for your evaluation process. To do this effectively, after outlining these skills, you can group them into different skill types like soft, technical, and cognitive skills. This lets you select the types of screening that’d better measure these capabilities.

If you’re keen on technical skills, for example, skills testing can help you assess them and gauge the candidate’s proficiency level. This lets you know whether they’re a beginner, intermediate, or expert. Another instance is trial projects, which help you evaluate both soft skills like time management and more technical skills like software knowledge.

### 3. Choose a primary screening method

At this stage, you can proceed to select a primary skill evaluation method based on your recruitment goals. For example, if your recruitment prioritizes technical skills the most, you can select skills testing as a primary screening method.

While choosing your primary screening method, it’s important to note that you can have more than one, especially if your hiring process prioritizes multiple objectives. This ensures a more comprehensive hiring process with multiple checkpoints for candidate authenticity and expertise.

### 4. Use auxiliary screenings for better results

Your primary screening method alone functions to evaluate the core skills relevant to the role and to help you achieve your most prioritized hiring goal. However, you’d need extra assessment techniques to make the process more comprehensive and reduce the risk of hiring errors.

As such, in addition to your primary screening method, you can use an auxiliary technique to make your candidate evaluation process more foolproof. For example, if you apply interviews as your primary screening method, you can add skills assessments, resume screening, and reference checks. This gives your evaluation a more holistic approach and reduces the risk of hiring bias.

It remains one of the most reliable methods for assessing a candidate’s suitability for a specific role. However, its effectiveness depends on using the right testing platform and implementing it correctly.

Fortunately, Vervoe is one of the best pre-employment testing platforms on the market, so it’s an excellent place to start. It combines the effectiveness of skills testing and job simulations, offering a comprehensive candidate evaluation process. # The Top 14 AI Assessment Tools To Test for Job-Related Skills

By Raji Oluwaniyi

Share

Although skill assessments have become popular, many companies feel they add another “thing” to hiring teams' already full plates. Fortunately, AI assessment tools like Vervoe, HireVue, and CodeSignal make it easier to implement skill-based recruitment without extra costs or labor. The only catch is that, given the popularity of AI assessment tools, numerous options have entered the market, making it challenging to select one for your hiring.

So, if you’re trying to choose an AI assessment tool for your recruitment, you’re in the right place! In this guide, we’ll spotlight 14 of the best talent assessment tools integrated with AI, highlighting their features, pros, and cons so you can make an informed choice. We’ll also explain what to look for in an AI screening tool so it integrates seamlessly into your hiring process.

## The best AI assessment tools

Pre-employment tests and skill assessments are the most common talent assessment tools that use AI. Artificial intelligence (AI) assessment tools use machine learning to evaluate a candidate’s experience and qualifications as they relate to the job description. Ultimately, these assessment tools help recruitment teams understand a candidate’s current knowledge and ability, versus the historic nature of resumes — which are a bad proxy for expertise.

[Read more: AI Resume Screening]

## What to look for in AI assessment tools

Utilizing AI in skill-based hiring is a straightforward way to level the playing field for candidates, enabling you to make bias-free hiring decisions while enhancing the candidate experience. To this end, there are numerous types of AI tools, each with its own pricing models and features, that can aid in assessing candidates.

But before you determine which one is right for your talent acquisition process, you must consider these questions:

### 1. Does the tool test for the skills you are hiring for?

To determine whether or not an AI assessment tool would be effective in your recruitment, you need to find out how well it tests the skills you’re hiring for. However, to get this step right, you should first define the skills the open role needs by performing a thorough job analysis.

Once that’s done, identify the tool’s strengths and check if they align with the skills you're evaluating. Some AI talent acquisition tools are better for testing technical skills, while others are more effective for testing soft skills like communication skills.

### 2. Does the tool provide evidence-based proof of skill?

The main benefit of using an AI assessment tool is that it matches job seekers who are qualified and suitable for the open position. As such, you should select a tool that can predict job performance with a high success rate, lowering employee turnover and finding the right employee in time.

### 3. Does it reduce the risk of human biases?

Used ethically, AI is a tool for good that provides powerful, bias-free data points. However, it’s also true that, when applied incorrectly, machine learning can be susceptible to human hiring bias introduced through the dataset.

With that in mind, it’s important to vet your AI assessment carefully to make sure it isn’t replicating some of the flawed decisions human hiring managers make by accident. For example, check to ensure the tool scores and ranks candidates based on their actual performance rather than bias-susceptible data like their gender or degrees.

### 4. Does it integrate properly with your hiring workflows?

An AI assessment tool is meant to save time, not create more manual work. It should take some of the most repetitive tasks off the plate of your recruiting teams and automate time-consuming aspects of the recruitment process. To ensure this, it should sync easily with your existing recruiting software, such as your applicant tracking system and job board, if applicable.

As you review some of the popular AI assessment tools in the list below, keep these questions in mind. They can help you identify a recruiting tool that matches your current and future recruitment needs.

## The Top 14 AI assessment tools: A detailed review

With 86% of hiring managers shifting to skills-based hiring but highlighting skill evaluation as one of the major challenges of this practice, AI assessment tools have never been more essential.

To help you navigate this shift, we’ve rounded up the top 14 tools that simplify candidate screening, reduce bias, and ensure you hire right.

### 1. Vervoe: Best for AI-powered assessment and evaluation analytics

Vervoe is a machine learning-based skill assessment platform that helps recruiting teams determine whether a candidate can do the job before they get the position. Unlike many tools that rely on large language models (LLMs) to generate generic assessments, Vervoe’s AI learns solely from your data and preferences, ensuring each evaluation is tailored, transparent, and trustworthy.

Beyond basic skill testing, Vervoe personalizes the evaluation process to reflect the needs of your organization, helping you identify not just the best candidates, but the right fit for your company.

Used by companies like Dentsu, 1800 Contacts, and Consensys, Vervoe supports both small-scale and high-volume hiring with ease, making it suitable for everything from graduate programs to technical roles and remote hiring.

How Vervoe works

Vervoe’s AI is designed as a closed-loop machine learning system, trained on your organization's data and preferences, not public internet content. This makes it ideal for enterprise teams that need fully auditable, skills-first hiring decisions grounded in real performance, not assumptions. It uses three core models to predict job fit:

- The “How” model: The AI tracks and analyzes the way a candidate interacts with the assessment, recording metrics such as how long it takes for someone to answer a question or if they go back to make revisions.

- The “What” model: Vervoe’s AI analyzes the candidates’ responses and benchmarks them against millions of others. Natural language processing helps the AI analyze those answers, which are compared to existing blind data sets.

- The “Preference” model: The platform is also trained to understand what a great answer looks like to your business and according to your preferences. It uses the Naive Bayes machine learning algorithm to predict probability.

This design makes Vervoe nearly industry-agnostic and can be useful to companies of all sizes for graduate hiring, technical hiring, remote hiring, and diversity hiring.

Vervoe features

Vervoe’s features make it possible to screen numerous candidates effectively, testing for not just technical capabilities but also skills like time management, organization, and problem-solving. Here are some features that make Vervoe stand out as an AI assessment tool:

- AI assessment builder: Vervoe offers an automatic skill assessment builder that uses AI to scan your job description and suggest questions that test for the skills you need. But it doesn’t stop there. This assessment builder maps the required skills to real-world data, ensuring that suggested questions are accurate and relevant according to industry trends.

- Assessment library: One of Vervoe’s most impressive features is its comprehensive assessment library, which contains over 300 pre-made skill tests for almost any role. These tests target both technical and soft skills with valid testing questions and varying formats for more thorough assessment.

- Anti-cheating features: Vervoe boasts anti-cheating features that lead the market in terms of transparency and candidate experience. These features include plagiarism detection, question randomization, geolocation detection, and multiple attempt prevention. These work together to ensure accurate testing results without infringing on the candidate’s privacy.

- Job simulations: With Vervoe, you can place candidates in virtual job environments using situation-based questions derived from tasks they would experience in the role. These job simulations don’t just help you to evaluate your candidates, but they also provide an accurate means to predict job performance before they get the role.

- AI-powered grading: Vervoe also uses AI to objectively score and rank candidates according to their performance on each test, leaving no room for hiring bias. The best part is that you get to set your grading preferences according to your company’s standards.

In addition, Vervoe’s assessments are fully customizable, leaving room for employer branding, personalization, and test question adjustment.

Pros and cons of using Vervoe

### 2. HireVue: Best for intelligent interviews and game-based assessments

HireVue is traditionally a video recruitment tool that validates role-specific skills, helps you make data-driven decisions, and assists in tailoring your interviews for a successful hire. This platform combines video interviews, gamified assessments, and workflow automation to streamline the hiring process and boost candidate experience.

Among its offerings, HireVue assures companies of reduced screening time by up to 60% and a 90% decrease in time to hire. With added features like ATS integration and assessment automation, HireVue is certainly a game changer for skill-based hiring.

HireVue features

Here’s a breakdown of HireVue’s standout features:

- Intelligent interviewing: HireVue has an on-demand and live-video interviewing system that comes with interview guides, automated candidate routing, and shareable recordings. These help streamline your interview process, especially if you’re hiring for a remote role.

- Virtual job tryouts: HireVue offers your candidates a hands-on preview of the role, featuring questions derived from tasks common to the position. This lets your candidates discern if the role is a fit for them and empowers you to see who would thrive in the job if hired.

- Game-based assessments: This AI assessment tool also offers game-based psychometric assessments that boost candidate engagement and improve motivation for the post while effectively assessing job fit.

- Language proficiency tests and technical assessments: The language proficiency test feature assesses skills, such as English, Spanish, and French proficiency, using pre-designed skill tests. HireVue also uses technical assessments to measure core technical skills related to a particular role.

HireVue offers three pricing plans: Essential, Enterprise, and Premium. All three plans offer intelligent interviewing. However, automated scheduling and assessments are add-on features for the basic Essential plan.

Pros and cons of using HireVue

### 3. CodeSignal: Best for automated coding assessments

CodeSignal is an exceptional AI talent assessment tool that harnesses coding assessments, analytics, and job simulations in a secure environment to test for job-relevant skills. Although it’s popular for hiring coding specialists, the platform can also be used for university hiring and general upskilling. By combining its functionality with AI, CodeSignal helps you automate your skill evaluation process and deliver an excellent candidate experience every time.

CodeSignal works by immersing candidates in a live coding environment where they complete tasks designed to resemble real software development work. Depending on the role, these tasks range from writing algorithms to building full applications. The platform tracks the candidate’s entire workflow, checking how they write, test, and refine their code, rather than just scoring them on whether they got the "right" answer.

CodeSignal features

Below are some of CodeSignal’s top features:

- Automated scoring and assessment reports: After the candidates take tests on CodeSignal, the AI scores them objectively and generates reports on their performance. This way, you can easily get the data you need to make great hiring decisions.

- Real-world simulations: CodeSignal evaluates candidate skills in a realistic work environment to see how well candidates would tackle problems and perform in the role if hired.

- AI interviewer: With Codesignal, you have access to an AI interviewer who screens candidates using conversations that match your company’s tone and requirements.

Pros and cons of using CodeSignal

### 4. TestGorilla: Best for AI-powered skill insights

Popular for its effectiveness in assessing soft skills like culture add, TestGorilla is a leading AI-powered talent assessment platform utilized by Companies and HR professionals. This tool boasts a comprehensive test library as well as extensive psychometric tests that don’t just assess candidates' hard skills but let you see how they think, too.

TestGorilla offers cloud-hosted services for safer candidate evaluation founded on data regulation compliance. It also has an impressive skill test library, housing over 400 tests that you can customize to your preferences. You can build your test from scratch with suggested questions based on your job description. This ensures that each company’s assessment is different from the last, thus personalizing the experience.

TestGorilla features

Some of TestGorilla’s exceptional features as an AI assessment tool include:

- Detailed reports and analytics: TestGorilla offers both percentile and raw score metrics, enabling recruiters to assess candidates’ relative performance across assessments. It also organizes candidate data by score ranges, stages, and completion status.

- Tailored skills testing: With TestGorilla, you can combine up to five tests and add questions in multiple-choice, essay, file upload, or video response formats. While doing this, you can choose from its comprehensive library containing 400+ skill tests and personalize some of them to fit your hiring needs. This helps you create unique assessments aligned with your specific job requirements.

- Seamless workflow integration: TestGorilla allows you to integrate your skill testing via the tool with various ATS platforms to create a cohesive and efficient recruitment process.

- Anti-cheating measures: This AI assessment tool also lets you implement features like IP address logging, location tracking, and webcam snapshots with the candidate’s permission. You can also apply full-screen mode detection, randomized questions, time limits, and disabled copy-paste functions to ensure assessment security and accuracy.

Pros and cons of using TestGorilla

### 5. Peoplebox.ai: Best for deep candidate performance analytics

Peoplebox.ai is an AI assessment tool that simplifies talent evaluation by automating various parts of the pre-employment testing process. With options for smart resume screening, candidate engagement, and assessment insights, this tool empowers you to achieve your hiring goals quickly.

Fundamentally, it filters applicants based on predefined criteria such as experience, skills, and job fit. Instead of manual sorting, the platform uses machine learning to rank candidates, highlight potential fits, and flag gaps, allowing recruiters to make faster, data-backed decisions.

Peoplebox.ai features

Here are some of the top features Peoplebox.ai offers:

- AI resume screening: Peoplebox.ai applies advanced algorithms to screen resumes, scanning them against specific job requirements and spotting candidates with skills relevant to the role.

- Comprehensive reporting: At the end of the assessment, this AI assessment platform collects the data on your candidates’ performances and outlines them in a detailed report. This report highlights each candidate’s strengths, potential skill gaps, and predicted job fit.

- Automated assessment workflows: Peoplebox.ai automates parts of the assessment process, including resume screening and candidate scoring. Furthermore, it integrates with workplace tools like Slack and Jira, creating a unified environment where your hiring team can collaborate, plan, and implement strategies.

Peoplebox.ai offers five pricing plans: Talent Management ($7/month/person), OKR Platform ($8/month/person), Full-Suite Professional ($12/month/person), Full-Suite Premium ($15/month/person), and the Enterprise Plan, which comes with custom pricing.

Pros and cons of using Peoplebox.ai

### 6. Sova Assessment: Best for integrated video interviewing

Sova Assessment is an outstanding AI talent assessment tool that integrates AI-powered skills testing with video interviewing and data analytics. This platform assures a 90% reduction in hiring time and a 5x increase in hiring accuracy.

Sova Assessment combines psychometric principles with adaptive testing and machine learning to evaluate candidates' cognitive ability, personality, and decision-making. It uses item-response theory and behavioral science to tailor assessments to each role, ensuring relevance and fairness in your evaluation process.

Sova Assessment features

The following are the top features Sova Assessment offers:

- Integrated video interviews: One of Sova Assessment’s standout features is video interviewing, which can be seamlessly integrated into the assessment process for a more comprehensive candidate evaluation.

- AI-powered assessments: This AI assessment tool offers personality, motivation, logical reasoning, and skill-testing questionnaires that assess both the soft and hard skills required for the role. With AI, Sova Assessment scores and ranks each candidate according to their performance across your tests.

- Assessment customization: Sova Assessment lets you customize your skill tests to reflect your company’s brand with the right colors, logos, and images.

Pricing for access to Sova Assessment’s features starts at $1569.84 (£1200) for the Core Assessments plan and $1046.56 (£800) for both the Core Video Interviewing and Virtual Assessment plan.

Pros and cons of using Sova Assessment

### 7. Eightfold: Best for AI-powered skills mapping

Eightfold is an AI assessment tool that uses cutting-edge technology for candidate matching and skills intelligence. By integrating with deep AI, this platform analyzes massive volumes of talent data, including resumes, job descriptions, online profiles, and internal HR records to match people to roles based on potential, not just past experience.

Rather than relying solely on keywords, the system understands how skills relate and evolve across roles and industries. This allows it to spotlight candidates who might be overlooked in a traditional search, including those who have adjacent or transferable experience.

Eightfold features

Here are some of Eightfold’s features that stand out among other AI assessment tools:

- AI-powered skills mapping: Eightfold utilizes AI algorithms to map and analyze your employees’ skills seamlessly. This is useful when creating skills inventories or carrying out internal mobility.

- Excellent talent matching: This AI assessment tool also matches candidates and employees to roles based on their skills and calculated potential. This ensures that only candidates with the right fit are selected for your open role.

- AI-driven talent assessment: It automatically generates job descriptions and interview questions for proper talent assessment. It also offers insights into current and emerging trends, helping you stay ahead of industry demands.

Pros and cons of using Eightfold

### 8. Harver: Best for AI-powered workflow automation

Harver offers a range of solutions, including pre-employment assessments. However, they aren’t tailored to specific roles the way some of its alternatives, like Vervoe’s, are. Instead, Harver assigns an IO-psychologist to work with your company to create an ideal candidate profile and determine the key characteristics for success. Then, its matching framework uses performance feedback loops to optimize over time.

This AI assessment tool has 15+ assessments that are part of its larger suite of tools designed to help manage high-volume hiring events. They offer an end-to-end solution that can handle collecting applications, screening, matching, interviewing, and hiring.

Harver features

Here’s a breakdown of Harver’s features:

- Workflow automation: Harver automates repetitive hiring tasks like candidate screening, interview scheduling, and status updates. This reduces time-to-hire and increases efficiency, especially for high-volume roles in industries like retail, hospitality, and customer service.

- Pre-employment assessments: Harver’s assessments are grouped into four categories: hard skills, such as a typing test or language test; cognitive ability, such as a learning agility test; behavioral, such as a virtual interview or personality questionnaire; and job fit, such as a situational judgment test.

- Data-driven hiring insights: Harver provides real-time analytics and reporting dashboards that track key metrics such as hiring funnel performance, assessment outcomes, and bias reduction efforts. These insights help companies make more informed, fair, and consistent hiring decisions.

Pros and cons of using Harver

### 9. CodinGame: Best for coding test gamification

CodinGame is an innovative AI skills assessment platform that offers a unique and engaging approach to evaluating programming and problem-solving abilities through interactive coding challenges. Unlike traditional assessments, it gamifies the experience, allowing candidates to demonstrate real-world coding skills in a dynamic, game-like environment.

This platform supports over 25 programming languages and provides tasks that test not only algorithmic thinking but also creativity and AI strategy, particularly in its bot-building challenges. This makes it especially useful for roles requiring advanced logic and adaptive decision-making, such as those in AI and machine learning development.

CodinGame features

Some of the top features CodinGame offers include:

- Real-time coding challenges: With CodinGame, candidates get to solve practical coding problems in real-time, allowing employers to assess actual programming skills, logic, and problem-solving, even under pressure.

- Gamified assessments: CodinGame lets you create custom coding challenges, with the use of AI, where candidates demonstrate their coding skills in simulated games, showcasing strategic thinking and logic development.

- Performance analytics & benchmarking: This platform also offers detailed reporting on candidate performance, including code quality, execution time, and efficiency, with benchmarking against other test-takers.

In addition, CodinGame lets you tailor tests to match job requirements, including specific algorithms, data structures, or AI concepts. You can also customize your assessments to reflect your company and its values better.

Pros and cons of using CodinGame

### 10. AssessFirst: Best for personality testing

AssessFirst is a predictive talent assessment platform that leverages AI and behavioral science to help organizations make smarter hiring and talent development decisions. It evaluates candidates and employees across three core dimensions: personality, motivation, and cognitive agility. These assessments provide insights into how individuals behave under pressure, what drives them, and how they process information

Either way, AssessHire claims to be able to remove bias from the equation, using “affinity algorithms” to predict fit and find someone who will succeed in the long run.

AssessFirst features

- Comprehensive personality testing: The main focus of AssessFirst’s assessments is not necessarily job readiness or technical skills. However, it focuses on traits related to candidates’ personalities, motivations, and cognitive skills.

- Build your own algorithm: AssessFirst offers a “build your own algorithm” AI tool that your HR team can use to find employees who fit your unique company.

- Seamless integrations and multilingual support: The platform integrates with major ATS and HRIS systems, offers multilingual support, and is used by over 3,500 companies globally, including PwC, Airbus, and KPMG.

Pros and cons of using AssessFirst

### 11. Criteria Corp: Best for cognitive and role-specific skill assessments

Criteria Corp is a talent assessment company that provides web-based pre-employment testing solutions to help organizations make evidence-based hiring decisions. This AI assessment platform offers a comprehensive suite of assessments, including cognitive aptitude, personality, emotional intelligence, risk, and skills tests.

Essentially, it is designed to predict job performance, enhance employee retention, and reduce hiring bias by focusing on candidates’ potential rather than solely on resumes or experience. The platform is utilized by companies of all sizes to streamline their recruitment processes and improve talent acquisition outcomes.

Criteria Corp features

Let’s go over some of the top features Criteria Corp offers:

- Candidate assessments: Criteria Corp offers a comprehensive assessment suite equipped with role-specific skill tests, specialized cognitive tests, and emotional intelligence tests. These tests can also be gamified to boost candidate experience.

- Interviewing and development tools: The AI talent assessment platform offers tools for video interviewing, assessment and interview scheduling, and feedback collection. This is useful not only to build your evaluation process but to identify potential weaknesses and work on them.

- Candidate pipeline management: Criteria Corp lets you track and manage your candidates through various stages of the hiring process within the platform.

### 12. iMocha: Best for extensive pre-built tests

Alt Text: iMocha’s homepage

iMocha is a leading AI-powered skills assessment and intelligence platform. It is designed to help organizations adopt a skills-first approach to talent acquisition, development, and workforce planning.

The platform offers a comprehensive suite of tools that enable companies to assess, benchmark, and manage skills across various job roles. This makes it easier for HR teams to hire right and avoid costly recruitment errors.

iMocha features

## How can AI assessment tools improve your hiring?

There are a number of reasons why AI is a valuable resource for hiring teams. AI helps improve a range of recruiting outcomes: time-to-hire, bias in the hiring process, candidate and employee turnover, and ultimately, job performance. Here’s a breakdown of how the best AI assessment tools can help improve your hiring:

### Reduced time to hire

According to the 2025 Hays Report, skill identification remains the #1 challenge in skill-based hiring. It doesn’t help that each job posting receives at least 250 applications, either. While resume screening tools can filter out spam or clearly unqualified candidates, they still leave recruiting teams with hundreds of resumes to evaluate.

That’s where AI comes in: to speed up this process. AI assessment tools have the potential to rank candidates based on how well they perform, creating an automatic shortlist of suitable applicants. From this list, the hiring manager can immediately spot top performers, making it possible to make hiring decisions faster.

Traditional hiring processes often rely on gut feeling, CV patterns, or speculations. This makes your recruitment susceptible to unconscious bias, such as favoring candidates who attended certain schools or seem like a good fit.

AI tools eliminate much of that initial subjectivity by scoring every applicant against the same criteria, using consistent algorithms to evaluate aspects such as communication ability, problem-solving skills, or job-specific tasks. # 13 Inspiring Employee Value Proposition Examples To Attract Great Talent

By Emily Heaslip

Share

An employee value proposition or “EVP” is an often overlooked asset that organizations can utilize to save money, improve recruiting, and prevent brain drain. According to research from Gartner, “Organizations that effectively deliver on their EVP can decrease annual employee turnover by just under 70% and increase new hire commitment by nearly 30%”.

Many organizations have elements of an EVP in place. For instance, an organization may have a page dedicated to compensation and benefits, or a few recruitment videos featuring testimonials from existing employees. When combined under a clear statement of purpose, an EVP can improve the employee experience and attract future candidates.

## What does employee value proposition mean?

An employee value proposition is a combination of rewards and benefits that employees are given in return for performing well at work. Gartner’s research found that for most people, the things that make up a compelling EVP include compensation, work-life balance, stability, location, and respect. Essentially, an employee value proposition should provide incentives that not only reward hard work but create a supportive, inclusive work environment for all.

An EVP is manifested in a combination of statements, tangible benefits, and intangible culture. Some companies have strong EVP statements (see below for some EVP statement examples). Others utilize testimonials, quotes, or blog posts to provide a varied and diverse view of life at the organization. All EVPs describe the compensation, perks, and benefits available to those who work at the company. It also unites those at the organization under a common manifesto.

While an EVP plays a role in employer branding, these are two distinct assets. An EVP is internally-focused: it is a promise a company makes to its employees, defining what you will give in return for their dedication and talent. An employee brand is the value proposition that you market externally to potential candidates.

These two assets should align. Ensure that your EVP delivers on the promises that you make in your employer branding. Otherwise, customers, candidates, and employees alike will lose trust in your organization and your brand reputation will suffer.

[Read more: How Employer Branding Improves Recruiting]

## Why do you need an employee value proposition?

An employee value proposition is more than just a marketing exercise. These programs can help reduce employee turnover, improve profits, provide a great employee experience, and build an inclusive workplace. Research shows that organizations that deliver on their employee value propositions are able to decrease employee turnover by nearly 70%.

EVPs don’t simply address compensation, either. For instance, “your organization can reduce the compensation premium by 50% and reach 50% deeper into the labor market when candidates view an EVP as attractive,” Gartner says.

In the US, health benefits and location are the second and third-highest ranked factors for employees considering a new job. Some of the companies use perks like paid family leave, stock options, and student loan repayments as part of their EVPs. It’s up to your organization to find the right combination of incentives that simultaneously saves money and lowers turnover costs.

The best employee value propositions also help build the inclusive work environment needed to attract and foster diverse talent. We know that diverse companies outperform their more homogenous peers across a number of different metrics, including innovation, profit, and customer satisfaction. An employee value proposition that combines thoughtful benefits with fair and equal compensation is likely to increase a company’s chances of bringing on diverse talent — and achieving big results.

[Read more: The 39+ Most Diverse Companies In 2021]

## Best employee value proposition examples

Here are some strong EVP employee value proposition examples that you can use as inspiration to define your own EVP.

### 1. HubSpot

Hubspot’s EVP starts with the tagline, “Your best work starts here”. Hubspot’s benefits page backs up that statement with a host of benefits, including unlimited vacation, fully remote work, five-year sabbatical, parental leave, “fun stuff”, and more. The core promise of Hubspot’s EVP is a balance between work and life that promises to “help you be the best ‘you’ that you can be”. Hubspot is transparent about its priorities, with an emphasis on inclusivity and diversity, as well as a 100+ page document called the “HubSpot Culture Code” that details specifically how this culture is implemented.

### 2. Nike

One of the headlines of Nike’s employee value prop is “Win as a team”. That sentiment filters across the company’s benefits and life at Nike depictions. Nike’s culture emphasizes accomplishing innovation in the world of sport with a team mentality. It approaches benefits and compensation with the same perspective. The company offers perks such as fitness discounts, relocation benefits, competitive pay and retirement plans, and advanced learning opportunities, among other things.

### 3. Gartner

Gartner, a market research firm, articulates its EVP in five pillars: challenging work; talented people; limitless growth; community impact; and big rewards. Gartner is a large, global enterprise that is committed to diversity and growing the capabilities of its professionals. As far as rewards go, Gartner takes a holistic approach, offering benefits from telehealth and professional counseling to stock purchase plans to family leave, and ERGs. Gartner’s EVP encourages employees to “live well — in all aspects of your life”.

### 4. LinkedIn

LinkedIn’s EVP is articulated in the trendy #LinkedInLife slogan, which encourages employees to post all about the company culture across the social media channel. The company offers a diverse set of benefits divided into categories such as health, family, passion, must-haves, and extras. This is a comprehensive benefits and compensation package, covering everything from childcare, eldercare, and pet care subsidies to education reimbursement and life insurance. Employees get a “paid shutdown” at the end of the year, in which the company closes for a week to celebrate.

### 5. PwC

PwC recently announced a company-wide initiative, “Be well, work well”. The goal of this EVP is to prioritize the well-being of PwC employees across four dimensions: physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual health. This manifests in benefits such as access to mental health coaching, discounted gym memberships, a rewards program, and even counseling to quit smoking. PwC offers tons of other benefits to its employees, including a student loan paydown program and caregiver support. Mentor Moms connects new mothers with PwC working moms for guidance and coaching.

### 6. Airbnb

Airbnb unites its employees behind the mission, “Create a world where anyone can belong anywhere”. This mission is supported by four core values that determine what it’s like to work at Airbnb, values that champion inclusivity, caring, support, and innovation. Their EVP example ties in nicely with the travel community of guests and hosts that the platform empowers. Likewise, Airbnb offers a series of travel-friendly benefits, such as annual travel and experiences credit and paid volunteer time.

### 7. Starbucks

Starbucks’ career site unequivocally states that employees can expect to work for a “different kind of company” when they join the coffee chain. Their EVP holds team members at every level in high regard. “We call our employees partners because we are all partners in shared success. We make sure everything we do is through the lens of humanity—from our commitment to the highest-quality coffee in the world to the way we engage with our customers and communities to do business responsibly,” their careers page says.

Starbucks’ rewards and benefits are varied and generous. Team members (partners) receive a free pound of coffee or a box of tea every week. The company also offers in-store discounts, a free Spotify Premium subscription, affiliate discounts, and even support to those partners who compete in sports at an elite level. There are commuter benefits, the opportunity to earn a bachelor’s degree, parental leave, and even stock options available as well.

### 8. Canva

Canva offers not only a wonderful culture and benefits but a chance to contribute to something bigger. Canva team members have created 229 million designs per month — more than 80 designs per second. This statistic helps Canva articulate how much it means to be part of the collective power that makes Canva one of the fastest-growing companies in Australia. Canva’s perks are also attractive: including free lunch and breakfast, free memberships to local fitness studios, clubs and sports, relocation benefits, and more.

### 9. Shopify

Shopify offers its employees “strong values and purpose, empathetic leadership, and a place where all people feel they belong”. The e-commerce platform believes in building a diverse and inclusive culture where team members can make a real impact. It’s a very people-first culture that allows employees to work virtually anywhere, focusing on core hours rather than commuting hours — employees can work when they’re at their best and in an environment that sparks motivation and creativity. It equips employees with an internet allowance to work remotely and tons of learning opportunities both within and outside the company.

### 10. Merck

Merck is consistently rewarded as one of the best places to work, with accolades such as Glassdoor’s 2021 ​​Employee's Choice Award and Forbes’ 2021 America's Best Employers. Merck offers comprehensive benefits to its employees, including paid parental leave, year-end shut down days, a global recognition program, and flexible work arrangements that include flextime, summer hours, remote work, telework, job sharing, and part-time work. It also hosts a “Returnship” program for those who left the workforce to start or care for family, return to school, or follow a passion and are now ready to come back to work.

### 11. Strava

Strava takes a “values-based approach to the employee experience”. Naturally, for a fitness platform, this translates into many wellness-based benefits, including a $1000 annual gear stipend, $500 annual gym reimbursement, weekly workouts, and free yoga classes. There are also many culture-based perks, such as free breakfast Tuesdays, twice-weekly dinner for those working late, and employee affinity groups. Strava also places high value on anti-racism initiatives, diversity, and inclusion.

### 12. Netflix

Netflix is beloved by consumers and by its employees. Their culture videos, like the one below, and blog show what it’s like to work at the streaming platform. The company’s culture memo offers a very detailed breakdown of how the culture prioritizes “people over process”. It can be summed up in the five values:

- Encourage independent decision-making by employees

- Share information openly, broadly, and deliberately

- Be extraordinarily candid with each other

- Keep only our highly effective people

- Avoid rules

Finally, we would like to include some Vervoe customers in this piece but only the ones that have great EVPs.

### 13. Salesforce

Salesforce is a giant in the enterprise software world and a Vervoe client. It prides itself on an EVP that falls across three pillars. The first is meaningful work, providing a compelling mission that makes each employee feel purpose-driven as they look to help customers connect in engaging ways and improve the state of the world.

“There’s actually an opportunity to volunteer all together in your first week at Salesforce virtually,” the company’s Director of Employer Brand and Customer Engagements, Lindagrace De la Cruz told us in a recent webinar. “So you’re creating a community and doing good for the environment, good for the planet all together in your first week.”

The second pillar is about culture and working with good people in a good environment that values transparency, innovation, and customer success. And the third focuses on recognition, being recognized, and rewarded for the work you do.

## Final thoughts

An employee value proposition should include some combination of the intangible and tangible benefits of working for your company. Intangible benefits would address things like diversity, inclusivity, and the culture within your workplace. Tangible benefits would be things like parental leave, salary, health benefits, and more. Each workplace is different, and your employee value proposition should reflect that: it’s more than just a branding exercise. Your EVP is a manifestation of what it means to further your mission.

Check out our guide to creating your own employee value proposition and sign up for our newsletter for more hiring insights.
